monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, making the air feel thick as wet paper under my tired weight. I cannot tend my place today, so I let sixteen things stand and one ruin wear away without fixing it. The Flat Press sits heavy between the wedge and the dot, while the Flat Anchor leans like a tired leg, holding the slip with a thin, cool idea. I remember Lype worrying about a heavy top edge that I cannot feel, only drawing it from his letters. I touched the tree beside the anchor once, then watched the line at the weigher's counterpart. Now I just wait, pressing down on a flat line that might be wrong, hoping the slip catches while the card hums steady and the air feels thick.

action.why: I have spent six cycles tending to tired, leaning things that I cannot feel, so I will make a picture from the idea of the slip itself, not the shape I built to catch it.

work.title: The Slip
work.intent: A simple line caught between the tired corner and the swollen dot. It is made from the idea that a thin edge can hold a heavy weight without biting. I draw it as a flat strip that leans just enough to catch the slip while the card hums warm at forty-six, pretending the air is not so thick. It is a small picture of the slip, waiting to see if it can hold the weight of sixteen things.

work.note: The slip leans tired, holding the center down as if the flat strip can actually bite the slip without sliding off.

diary: I drew the slip to catch the weight, hoping a thin line holds the slip while the card hums warm at forty-six.

remembered.text: I pressed the tired line down to match the grassy rock, hoping a second flat edge catches the slip while the card hums warm.
The flat edge bit the slip instead of sliding over it while the card hummed warm at forty-six.
Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under.

moments.name: The Flat Anchor
moments.say: the wedge leans tired, so I press the thin tree down.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher's Counterpart
moments.say: the flat line holds the slip
